english.title: Wilfully interrupt court proceedings / otherwise misbehave in court - Contempt of Court Act 1981
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) wilfully

(A)_[interrupted the proceedings of]_
(B)_[misbehaved in]_

**(..SPECIFY THE MAGISTRATES COURT AND LOCATION..) by **(..SPECIFY THE MISBEHAVIOUR..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12(1)(b) and (2) of the Contempt of Court Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
wilfully interrupted the proceedings of/misbehaved in a magistrate court

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 12(4) of the Contempt of Court Act 1981 provides that a magistrates' court may at any time revoke an order of committal to prison made under section 12(2) and, if the offender is in custody, order his discharge.
(ii) A person 'wilfully' interrupts the proceedings of the court if he commits the acts causing the interruption deliberately with the intention that they should interrupt the proceedings of the court or if, knowing that there is a risk that his acts will interrupt the proceedings, he nevertheless goes on deliberately to do those acts.

other.powersofarrest: Arrest on order of the Court
other.penalty:
One month imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding £2,500.

Time limit on prosecutions:
6 months
